1. Model consistently underestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially when recent history shows downward trends — adjust downward bias by 2–5% for 1–3 day horizons.

2. Model overestimates prices after sharp spikes (e.g., >70) — reduce forecast by 5–15% for 1–2 day post-spike periods.

3. Model exhibits mean reversion bias — if 30-day history shows strong upward trend, forecast should not overshoot 10% above recent peak; if downward, avoid dropping below 5% below recent trough.

4. Forecast lag: if true outcome is >10% higher than 30-day history, model often lags by 1–3 days — adjust forecast to align with 3-day moving average of true values.

5. Model overreacts to short-term volatility — avoid sharp upward moves unless confirmed by 2+ consecutive days of rising prices; use 5-day smoothing for volatility-sensitive forecasts.

6. For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate true mean — add 3–7% to forecast to align with historical mean of last 60 days.

7. When true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% for 3+ consecutive days, model is likely underestimating supply/demand fundamentals — increase forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
